body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the observable augmented moment system \(S(x)=\{P(A=a,Z=z\mid X=x)\}_{a,z}\) and \(T_u(x)=E_P\{h_{0,u}(Y)e_Ae_Z^{\mathsf T}\mid X=x\}\), \(u=1,\ldots,K\), identifies \((\pi,M_A,M_Z,\Gamma_Y)\) up to a common permutation; together with the full observed conditional density \(p_A(y\mid x)\), it identifies \(f(y\mid x)=\Pi^{-1}M_A^{-1}p_A(y\mid x)\). The modal margin selects the unique ordered labeling, and \(\psi_j=E_P\{m_j(X)\}=E\{Y(j)\}\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).
body.justification: This isolates point identification from the later efficiency claim and fixes the causal meaning of each recovered class.
body.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes identify factors up to labels, while Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen give the binary hidden-treatment version; the conditional measurable \(K\)-class formulation must be verified on the stated quantitative stratum.
body.consumer: It makes the six maternal-smoking exposure levels interpretable as ordered intervention states rather than anonymous mixture classes.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a version of every conditional law and fix \(x\) outside the common null set in the assumptions.  Write \(A_0=M_A(x)\), \(Z_0=M_Z(x)\), \(\gamma_j=\Gamma_Y(x)_{\cdot j}\), and \(\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\{\pi(x)\}\).  By conditional three-view independence,
\[
 S=A_0\Pi Z_0^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 T_u=A_0\Pi\operatorname{diag}(\gamma_{u1},\ldots,\gamma_{uK})Z_0^{\mathsf T}. \tag{1}
\]
The three rank assumptions and latent positivity make \(A_0,Z_0,\Pi\), and \(\Gamma_Y(x)\) invertible.  Hence \(S\) is invertible, and (1) gives the observable simultaneous-similarity family
\[
 T_uS^{-1}=A_0\operatorname{diag}(\gamma_{u1},\ldots,\gamma_{uK})A_0^{-1},\qquad u=1,\ldots,K. \tag{2}
\]
Because \(\Gamma_Y(x)\) is invertible, its columns are distinct and the diagonal matrices in (2) span the full diagonal algebra.  Consequently the common one-dimensional invariant subspaces of the algebra generated by \(\{T_uS^{-1}:u\le K\}\) are exactly \(\operatorname{span}(A_{0,\cdot j})\), \(j=1,\ldots,K\).  This proves recovery of the columns of \(A_0\) up to scaling and permutation.  Each column is a probability vector, so \(\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}A_{0,\cdot j}=1\) fixes its scale.

Put \(H=A_0^{-1}S=\Pi Z_0^{\mathsf T}\).  Since every column of \(Z_0\) sums to one,
\[
 H\mathbf 1_K=\Pi Z_0^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_K=\pi(x),
 \qquad
 Z_0^{\mathsf T}=\Pi^{-1}H. \tag{3}
\]
Thus (3) recovers \(\pi(x)\) and \(Z_0\) under the same permutation.  Finally, (1) yields
\[
 \operatorname{diag}(\gamma_{u1},\ldots,\gamma_{uK})
 =\Pi^{-1}A_0^{-1}T_u(Z_0^{\mathsf T})^{-1}, \tag{4}
\]
which recovers \(\Gamma_Y(x)\).

For the full outcome law, let \(p_A(y\mid x)\) be the \(K\)-vector whose \(a\)-th coordinate is the conditional joint density of \((Y,A=a)\) given \(X=x\).  Conditional independence gives
\[
 p_A(y\mid x)=A_0\Pi f(y\mid x),
 \qquad
 f(y\mid x)=\Pi^{-1}A_0^{-1}p_A(y\mid x) \quad \nu\text{-a.e.} \tag{5}
\]
All inversions in (2)--(5) are legitimate by the displayed rank and positivity assumptions.  Matrix inversion is Borel measurable on the nonsingular matrices.  The common eigenspaces in (2) can be selected measurably by choosing, from a fixed countable dense set of coefficient vectors, the first linear combination having distinct eigenvalues; such a combination exists because the columns of \(\Gamma_Y(x)\) are distinct.  The modal inequality assigns recovered column \(j\) to the unique row at which it has its maximum; its positive margin makes this assignment unique and measurable.  Hence (2)--(5) define an observed-law recovery map, not a definition of the causal target.

By (5), \(m_j(x)=E(Y\mid J=j,X=x)\).  Consistency gives
\[
 E\{Y(j)\mid J=j,X=x\}=E(Y\mid J=j,X=x)=m_j(x). \tag{6}
\]
Latent ignorability gives \(E\{Y(j)\mid J=j,X=x\}=E\{Y(j)\mid X=x\}\); latent positivity makes the conditioning event available.  Taking \(P_X\)-expectations in (6) proves
\[
 E\{Y(j)\}=E_P\{m_j(X)\}=\psi_j.
\]
Thus the causal estimand is equal to the recovered observed-law functional under the declared causal assumptions.
